title: How pleasure club members dressed for parades
summary: Pleasure clubs bought new outfits each year: striped silk shirts, soft white hats and badges.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: The members of the clubs, lodges and all that, do they dress the same as they do today for parades? Do they wear the same kind of uniforms? What, the lodges? The lodges, yeah. The different clubs and stuff, pleasure clubs.

Oh, pleasure clubs? Well, no, pleasure clubs, I mean, like when they turned out, well, what was the pleasure club we could call now? Let me see, the Jolly Boys and what's the other ones down here, the name of them? Oh, there's several of them.
Huh? There's so many of them here and there.

The one that took a chase belongs to that. I don't know which one. Oh, I played at the parade last time. That was the last parade, I think. Anyway. Well, there was pleasure clubs. I mean, they always buy a uniform. Every year when they have a parade, they buy something different. And how would they dress?

Well, they dressed in silk shirts at the time. I remember the black striped silk shirts. I mean, that was the style of silk shirts at the time. I remember black striped silk shirts, maybe a pair of brown shards or something like that.

Huh? Ties? No, no ties. No, just open collar. They wear a cap or hat? No, no. One of them soft hats. White hats, soft. They always like you buy a little dollar brown hat today. I mean, you know, rag hats. White. And all of them had that. They had them on the side like that.
Had what on the—oh, the hats on the side. Yeah, hats on the side.
They turned out on the side. On the side like that.
Would they have any ribbons on or anything?
Oh, they had their badges, you know what I mean. Their badges. They had their badges.
And that signified they were a member of the club.

Oh, yeah, yeah. They all—they all—each one got his own—a new outfit every year. That's right. Same as like the Indians do, I mean with masses. They get a different outfit every year. They get the suits made. You know, I wear the same suit they don't want them. No one can recall if they wore that suit last year or not. But it's just the idea that they wanted something new.
